features.name: Any target you already shoot
features.sentence: Photograph or scan whatever you shot on, set the scale once, and mark the holes by hand, on the computer or on the phone under a crosshair that stays in the middle; place several bulls and keep the layout as a template for the next sheet. Finding the holes by itself on any target is the goal, not yet a feature.

features.note: On a target GroupLab did not print, you can now place each bull by hand

features.name: A GroupLab sheet reads itself
features.sentence: A printed GroupLab sheet names itself from its codes and is measured from its own markers, so nothing is set by hand.
features.note: A real scanned sheet is included in the download

features.name: Every hole found, and every one yours to change
features.sentence: Holes are found for you, and any one can be moved, added, removed, called a flyer or given a note.
features.note: You can now click a hole to edit it

features.name: The bulls you aimed at
features.sentence: Say which bulls you fired at, by rows, columns or a list, and each shot is measured from the bull it was aimed at.
features.note: You can now tell GroupLab which bulls you aimed at

features.name: A sheet shot off by the same amount
features.sentence: When every shot on a sheet of one shot per bull landed off by the same amount, as an unzeroed rifle does, each goes to the bull it was fired at.
features.note: When every shot on a sheet of one shot per bull landed off by the same amount

features.name: Works in your scope's unit
features.sentence: The first run asks whether your scope is in mil or MOA, each rifle keeps its own scope unit and click (0.1 mil, 0.05 mil, 1/4 MOA, 1/8 MOA or any other), and the zero correction, the clicks, the dope, the hit chance and group sizes as angles then read in that unit alone, with the other one tap away.
features.note: GroupLab now asks whether your scope is in mil or MOA
